title: add-geo-anchored-kms-consent-and-temporal-rbac-bindings
author: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a geo-anchored KMS consent enforcement proxy and RBACv2 temporal binding support so tenant-level geo residency assertions and short-lived operator grants can be evaluated consistently at request time. Motivation: customers with region-pinning requirements and strict key residency need a predictable enforcement point that both validates KMS usage against declared residency and emits audit-proof evidence without adding latency to the common path. This PR provides: 1) a KMS proxy that validates consent headers (tenant-provided consent+policy reference), resolves preferred CMK per-geo policy, and returns a proof token attached to the request context; 2) RBACv2 temporal bindings so operators can be granted transient, region-scoped roles (timeboxed with non-replayable nonce), integrating with the existing policy compiler; 3) audit enrichment that attaches residency-evidence and consent token hashes to signed audit envelopes; 4) migration scripts and an admin docs guide for operators to opt-in and for platform SREs to enable the proxy. Implementation notes: consent header format is backward-compatible (existing requests without consent still pass for non-sovereign tenants), enforcement is opt-in via a per-tenant flag. All behavior is gated behind feature flags and a circuit-breaker in the proxy to fail open if downstream KMS becomes unreachable. The description below includes high-level rollout and testing notes.

review_comments: Arjun: General +1 but please ensure the consent token TTL is documented and short-lived. Author reply: token TTL defaults to 5 minutes and is documented in docs/ops/kms-consent.md.

Lucia: Are we leaking any residency metadata in logs? Suggest redact by default. Author reply: added audit enricher that emits residency hash only; full metadata is only placed in signed audit envelopes stored in secure retention.

Samuel: Concerned about KMS fail-open semantics. Please add a circuit-breaker and telemetry. Author reply: circuit-breaker added in helm chart and metrics exposed (kms_proxy_failopen_count), SLOs documented.
Compliance review (Tina): Ensure proofs include signing key ID and proof version. Author reply: added proof v1 structure and signer key id; retention policy aligned with compliance playbook.

security-scan: warn(weak-kms-key-template) -> addressed in second commit
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2025-06-22 by Maya Chen. Forward-ported patch to release/2025-q3. Release note prepared and attached. Backports: none required for this week.
release_notes: Security: Adds per-tenant KMS consent enforcement proxy and RBACv2 temporal bindings to support geo-residency and short-lived operator grants. Admins must review tenant opt-in flags; see docs/ops/kms-consent.md for migration steps. Feature is disabled by default.
rationale: Customers operating under data residency or key-sovereignty constraints requested a single enforcement point that can both validate KMS usage policy and provide cryptographic evidence to auditors. RBAC temporal bindings reduce operator blast radius by limiting duration and scope of escalations. Combining both reduces manual post-hoc audits and prevents misrouted KMS traffic.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: enable feature flag for 5 internal tenants in staging for 72 hours, validate latency (<5ms added), audit envelope contents and SLI signals, then enable for customer opt-in cohorts. If error rate or kms_proxy_failopen_count exceeds threshold, rollback via feature flag. Full GA gate requires security-scan:pass and two-week production canary.
test_plan: Unit tests for consent parsing and policy resolution, integration tests covering KMS fail-open/fail-closed paths, RBAC policy compiler unit tests, end-to-end tests via tests/integration/kms_geo_consent_test.go. Added CI job to run security-scan and integration-kms on feature branch before merge.
